# Climate and air quality (/docs/air-quality)



The S1 Pro has two air sensors:

* the **SCD40**, a real CO₂ sensor (photoacoustic NDIR), for **CO₂**;
* the **BME688**, a gas sensor whose readings Bosch's BSEC software turns into an **air quality index (IAQ)**,
  an **air quality class**, a **VOC** estimate, and temperature, humidity and pressure.

## CO₂ [#co]

**CO₂** (ppm) is measured directly by the SCD40. It is the best indicator of how stale the air is in an occupied
room: people breathe out CO₂.

| CO₂ (ppm) | Typical meaning              |
| --------- | ---------------------------- |
| \~420     | Outdoor air                  |
| \< 800    | Well ventilated              |
| 800–1200  | Ventilation is getting short |
| > 1200    | Stuffy; ventilate            |

The official firmware turns the SCD40's automatic self-calibration **off** and compensates the reading with the
air pressure from the BME688. If the CO₂ reading drifts over the months (for example it never gets near \~420 ppm
with the windows wide open), use the [*Calibrate CO₂ sensor*](/docs/maintenance#calibrate-co2-sensor) maintenance
action.

## Air quality index (IAQ) [#air-quality-index-iaq]

**Air quality (IAQ)** is a number from 0 to 500 that Bosch's BSEC algorithm calculates from the BME688's gas
readings. It reacts to volatile compounds in the air: cooking, cleaning products, paint, perfume, people. Lower is
better.

The BME688 has no absolute scale: BSEC learns what clean and polluted air look like *in your room*, so the IAQ is
relative to the history of that room.

## Air quality class [#air-quality-class]

**Air quality** turns the IAQ into words. The sensor's firmware uses these ranges:

| Class                   | IAQ        |
| ----------------------- | ---------- |
| **Excellent**           | 0–50       |
| **Good**                | 51–100     |
| **Lightly polluted**    | 101–150    |
| **Moderately polluted** | 151–200    |
| **Heavily polluted**    | 201–250    |
| **Severely polluted**   | 251–350    |
| **Extremely polluted**  | 351 and up |

The [*Air quality changed*](/docs/flows#when) trigger and the [*Air quality is … or worse*](/docs/flows#and)
condition use these classes.

## Calibration [#calibration]

**Air quality calibration** tells you how reliable the IAQ, the class and the VOC are right now. It does not
measure anything itself.

| State           | Meaning                                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Stabilizing** | Just started; the gas sensor is still warming up. The values mean nothing yet. |
| **Uncertain**   | Too little history; the values are rough.                                      |
| **Calibrating** | BSEC is learning the room and getting better.                                  |
| **Calibrated**  | BSEC knows the room. IAQ, class and VOC are reliable.                          |

Getting to *Calibrated* takes hours to a few days. It goes fastest when the sensor experiences both fresh air
(a window open) and polluted air. After a power cut or restart the state can drop back a step.

CO₂ comes from the separate SCD40 and does **not** depend on this calibration.

## VOC [#voc]

**VOC** (ppm) is BSEC's estimate of the concentration of volatile organic compounds, derived from the same gas
readings as the IAQ. Use it as a trend ("something is going on in the kitchen") rather than as an absolute
measurement.

## Not shown on the device [#not-shown-on-the-device]

The sensor reports a few more air values that the app leaves off the tile on purpose:

| Entity on the sensor           | Why it is not shown                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| BME688 CO₂ equivalent          | An estimate from the gas sensor; the real CO₂ from the SCD40 is shown instead.       |
| BME688 gas resistance          | A raw value that BSEC already turns into IAQ and VOC.                                |
| SCD40 temperature and humidity | Duplicates of the BME688 values; the SCD40 uses them internally for its CO₂ reading. |


# Changelog (/docs/changelog)



{/* Generated from CHANGELOG.md by scripts/sync-changelog.mjs; edit that file instead. */}

All notable changes to this app are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and the app uses
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## \[Unreleased] [#unreleased]

### Changed [#changed]

* The app is now a Homey Python app on top of `homey-esphomedriver` (and `aioesphomeapi`) instead of
  `@2colors/esphome-native-api`. The library takes over the connection, reconnects, pairing (mDNS and *Add by IP…*)
  and the standard capabilities; sensors with an API encryption key can now be added.
* Presence is `alarm_presence` and movement is `alarm_motion` (was `alarm_motion` and `sensy_moving`).
  Existing sensors must be removed and added again.
* Requires Homey 13.0 or newer.
* App id is `io.github.starredev.sensy`, so later Sensy-One products can be added as drivers of the same app.
  The Node.js version (`io.github.starredev.sensys1pro`) is kept on the `node` branch and tag `node-1.0.0`.

### Added [#added]

* Diagnostic and configuration entities can be shown as capabilities from the device settings.
* *Refresh capabilities* maintenance action.
* Air quality class (*Excellent* … *Extremely polluted*), its calibration state and VOC as capabilities, with an
  *Air quality changed* trigger and an *Air quality is X or worse* condition.
* Tracking settings of the radar: holding people who stand still (the firmware's holding engine, off by default),
  stationary speed, hold after standing still, hold time and jump distance; light and UV offsets.
* Settings for mirrored mounting, real-time environment readings and the buzzer's pitch and volume.
* Maintenance actions: calibrate the CO₂ sensor, restart the sensor, restart the radar.
* The radar widget shows whether a person is moving, standing still or held.
* A device warning and a *New firmware is available* trigger when Sensy-One releases a newer firmware.
* Zone capabilities follow the zones drawn in the zone editor automatically.

## \[1.0.0] - unreleased [#100---unreleased]

### Added [#added-1]

* S1 Pro Multi Sense device, discovered through mDNS and followed when its IP address changes.
* Presence, movement and people count; temperature, humidity, pressure, IAQ, CO₂, light and UV.
* Up to three zones with presence, movement and people sub-capabilities, shown only for zones that have an outline.
* Flow cards: seven triggers, four conditions and two actions.
* Device settings that stay in sync with the sensor in both directions.
* Zone editor on the app settings page and the *Sensy radar* dashboard widget.
* Works with the official Sensy-One firmware as well as the Homey edition; live target positions are read from whichever the sensor provides.
* Adding a sensor by IP address or host name when mDNS discovery finds nothing.
* A device warning when the sensor's BLE proxy is switched on, since it makes the WiFi connection unstable and Homey does not use it.

### Changed [#changed-1]

* App id is `io.github.starredev.sensys1pro` (was `nl.bryan.sensys1pro` during development).
* Rewritten as layered, test-covered ES modules; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/starredev/homey-sensy-s1pro/blob/node/CONTRIBUTING.md).


# The device (/docs/device)



The **S1 Pro Multi Sense** device is a Homey *sensor*. Its tile shows the room's presence and climate; zones
appear as extra values for every zone you draw.

## Presence and people [#presence-and-people]

| Value        | Capability       | Meaning                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Presence** | `alarm_presence` | Someone is in the room, also when they sit or lie still. Stays on for the [presence hold time](/docs/settings#detection) after the last detection. |
| **Motion**   | `alarm_motion`   | Someone in the room is moving.                                                                                                                     |
| **People**   | `sensy_people`   | Number of people the radar tracks, 0 to 3.                                                                                                         |

Homey's **zone activity** reacts to both presence and motion sensors, so the room the device is in becomes
active as soon as the sensor sees someone, and stays active while they sit still.

<Callout type="info" title="Up to three people">
  The radar tracks at most three targets at a time. With more people in the room the count stays at 3.
</Callout>

## Climate and air [#climate-and-air]

| Value                       | Capability            | Source on the sensor      | Unit                               |
| --------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| **Temperature**             | `measure_temperature` | BME688                    | °C                                 |
| **Humidity**                | `measure_humidity`    | BME688                    | %                                  |
| **Pressure**                | `measure_pressure`    | BME688                    | mbar (= hPa)                       |
| **CO₂**                     | `measure_co2`         | SCD40 (a real CO₂ sensor) | ppm                                |
| **Air quality (IAQ)**       | `sensy_iaq`           | BME688 / Bosch BSEC       | 0–500 index                        |
| **Air quality**             | `sensy_air_quality`   | BME688 / Bosch BSEC       | *Excellent* … *Extremely polluted* |
| **Air quality calibration** | `sensy_iaq_accuracy`  | BME688 / Bosch BSEC       | *Stabilizing* … *Calibrated*       |
| **VOC**                     | `measure_tvoc`        | BME688 / Bosch BSEC       | ppm                                |
| **Luminance**               | `measure_luminance`   | LTR390                    | lx                                 |
| **Ultraviolet**             | `measure_ultraviolet` | LTR390                    | UV index                           |

The air quality values are explained in detail on the [Air quality](/docs/air-quality) page.

How often these values update depends on [*Real-time environment readings*](/docs/settings#detection): on (the
default) they follow every change, off they update once a minute.

## Zones [#zones]

For every zone you draw in the [zone editor](/docs/zones), three values appear:

| Value                | Capability                  | Meaning                        |
| -------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| **Zone N presence**  | `sensy_zone_presence.zoneN` | Someone is inside zone N       |
| **Zone N movement**  | `sensy_zone_movement.zoneN` | Someone moves inside zone N    |
| **People in zone N** | `sensy_zone_people.zoneN`   | Number of people inside zone N |

They appear a few seconds after you save a zone with at least three points, and disappear again when you clear
the zone. Zones you never drew do not clutter the tile.

## Maintenance actions [#maintenance-actions]

Open the device and look under maintenance (the wrench, or *Maintenance* in the device settings) for:

* **Calibrate CO₂ sensor**
* **Restart sensor**
* **Restart radar**
* **Refresh capabilities**

See [Maintenance and firmware](/docs/maintenance) for what they do and when to use them.

## Insights [#insights]

Presence, motion, people, all climate values and the zone values are logged in Homey **Insights**, so you can
see when a room was used and how CO₂ or humidity developed over the day. The air quality class and its
calibration state are text values and are not logged.

## Warnings on the device [#warnings-on-the-device]

The device can show a warning bar with one or more of these messages:

| Warning                     | What to do                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *The BLE proxy is on…*      | Turn off **BLE \| Proxy** on the sensor's web page; see [Requirements](/docs/installation#bluetooth-proxy). |
| *Firmware vX is available…* | A newer official firmware is out; see [Firmware updates](/docs/maintenance#firmware-updates).               |

## When the sensor is offline [#when-the-sensor-is-offline]

If the sensor stops answering, the device becomes **unavailable** with the message *ESPHome connection lost*.
The app reconnects by itself as soon as the sensor is back, also when it got a new IP address. Flows do not fire
for values that are merely re-sent after a reconnect.


# Flows (/docs/flows)



The device comes with two kinds of flow cards:

* **The app's own cards** for the room, zones, air quality and firmware, listed below.
* **Homey's standard cards** for the standard capabilities on the device, such as *Presence turned on* or *The
  CO₂ level changed*. You get these automatically. Every value of the device is also available as a token, so
  you can compare it in a *Logic* card.

The complete list with every argument and token is in the [flow card reference](/docs/reference/flow-cards).

## When… [#when]

| Card                            | Fires when                                                                                         | Tokens                         |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| **Someone became present**      | The room goes from empty to occupied.                                                              | *People*                       |
| **The room became empty**       | Nobody is left in the room (after the presence hold time).                                         |                                |
| **Number of people changed**    | The people count changes.                                                                          | *People*, *Previous*           |
| **Air quality changed**         | The [air quality class](/docs/air-quality) changes, for example from *Good* to *Lightly polluted*. | *Air quality*, *Previous*      |
| **Someone entered \[zone]**     | The zone goes from empty to occupied.                                                              | *People* (at least 1)          |
| **\[zone] became empty**        | Nobody is left in the zone (after the zone's hold time).                                           |                                |
| **Movement started in \[zone]** | Someone in the zone starts moving.                                                                 |                                |
| **Movement stopped in \[zone]** | Movement in the zone stops.                                                                        |                                |
| **New firmware is available**   | Sensy-One released a firmware newer than the sensor runs. Fires once per version.                  | *Version*, *Installed version* |

<Callout type="info" title="No false triggers after a reconnect">
  When the sensor reconnects it re-sends all its values. The app does not treat those as changes, so a
  reconnect never fires *someone became present*, *zone entered* or similar cards. Zone cards also never fire
  for zones that have no outline.
</Callout>

## And… [#and]

| Card                                           | True when                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Someone is / isn't present**                 | The room is occupied (or not).                                                       |
| **\[zone] is / isn't occupied**                | Someone is inside the zone (or not). Always false for a zone without an outline.     |
| **There is / is no movement in \[zone]**       | Someone moves inside the zone (or not).                                              |
| **Number of people is / isn't above \[count]** | The people count is higher than *count* (0–3).                                       |
| **Air quality is / isn't \[level] or worse**   | The air is at least as polluted as *level*. False until the sensor reported a class. |

## Then… [#then]

| Card                                                        | What it does                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Set presence hold time of \[zone] to \[seconds] seconds** | Changes the zone's hold time on the sensor (0–3600 s). Handy to make a zone "stickier" at night.                 |
| **Beep for \[duration] seconds**                            | Sounds the buzzer for 0.1 to 5 seconds. Pitch and volume come from the [buzzer settings](/docs/settings#buzzer). |

## Examples [#examples]

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="Light on when someone sits down at the desk">
    * **When** *Someone entered* **Zone 1 (desk)**
    * **And** a *Logic* card: the device's *Luminance* token is less than 50
    * **Then** turn on the desk lamp

    And a second flow: **When** *Zone 1 became empty* **Then** turn off the desk lamp. Raise the zone's
    *presence hold time* if the lamp goes off while you are still reading.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Ventilation on high CO₂">
    * **When** *The CO₂ level changed* (Homey's standard card)
    * **And** a *Logic* card: the *CO₂* token is greater than 1000
    * **Then** set the ventilation to high

    With a separate flow back to normal below 800 ppm, so it does not switch on and off around one value.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Feed the sensor's readings to a ventilation system">
    Many ventilation systems accept external CO₂ and humidity values. Use **When** *The CO₂ level changed*
    **Then** *report the CO₂ level* with the device's *CO₂* token, and the same for humidity.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Bathroom light that stays on in the shower">
    * **When** *Someone became present* **Then** bathroom light on.
    * **When** *The room became empty* **Then** bathroom light off.
    * In the [device settings](/docs/settings#detection), set *Presence hold time* to a few minutes; the radar sees
      people in the shower, but water and glass can make detection patchy.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Warn when the air gets bad">
    * **When** *Air quality changed*
    * **And** *Air quality is* **Moderately polluted** *or worse*
    * **Then** send a notification: "Air quality is now \[Air quality], open a window."

    Right after the sensor started, the air quality is not calibrated yet; see
    [Air quality](/docs/air-quality#calibration). You can check the *Air quality calibration* token in a *Logic*
    card if you want to skip notifications until it shows *Calibrated*.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Night mode for a bedroom">
    * At 23:00: **Set presence hold time of Zone 1 (bed) to 1800 seconds**.
    * At 07:00: set it back to 120 seconds.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Know when the sensor has new firmware">
    **When** *New firmware is available* **Then** send a notification: "Sensy firmware \[Version] is out
    (installed: \[Installed version])."
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Tips [#tips]

* **Use zones rather than the room** when only part of a room matters; zone cards ignore what happens elsewhere.
* **Tune the hold times** before building complex flows; most "light goes off while I sit still" issues are a
  hold time that is too short.
* **Combine with luminance**: the sensor's own light reading tells you whether a light is needed.


# Introduction (/docs)



Sensy S1 Pro turns the [Sensy-One S1 Pro Multi Sense](https://github.com/sensy-one/S1-Pro-Multi-Sense) into a
native Homey device: presence that also sees people who sit still, up to three zones, the number of people in the
room, and CO₂, air quality, temperature, humidity, pressure, light and UV.

Homey talks to the sensor directly over the ESPHome native API on your local network. No Home Assistant, no MQTT
broker and no cloud.

<ThemedImage light="/images/radar-hero-light.svg" dark="/images/radar-hero-dark.svg" alt="The radar map with two zones, an exclusion zone and three people" />

<Callout type="info" title="Unofficial community project">
  This app is not made, endorsed or supported by Sensy-One. It works with the official Sensy-One firmware.
</Callout>

## What it does [#what-it-does]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Presence and people" href="/docs/device">
    Presence that stays on while you sit still, movement, and how many people are in the room.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Zones" href="/docs/zones">
    Draw up to three zones on a live radar map, each with its own presence, flows and settings.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Climate and air quality" href="/docs/air-quality">
    CO₂, an air quality index with a plain-language class, VOC, temperature, humidity, light and UV.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Radar widget" href="/docs/widget">
    A live top-down radar of the room on your dashboard.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Flows" href="/docs/flows">
    Triggers, conditions and actions for the room, every zone, air quality and new firmware.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Settings" href="/docs/settings">
    Every setting of the sensor, kept in sync in both directions.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Get started [#get-started]

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Check the requirements [#check-the-requirements]

    A Homey Pro (2023) or Homey Pro mini on Homey 13 or newer, and the S1 Pro on the official firmware.
    [Requirements](/docs/installation#requirements)
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Install the app and add the sensor [#install-the-app-and-add-the-sensor]

    Install **Sensy S1 Pro**, then add the sensor under **Devices → + → Sensy S1 Pro**.
    [Installation](/docs/installation)
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Draw your zones [#draw-your-zones]

    Open **Apps → Sensy S1 Pro → Configure** and draw zones while you walk through the room.
    [Zones](/docs/zones)
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Automate [#automate]

    Build [flows](/docs/flows) and add the [radar widget](/docs/widget) to a dashboard.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## How it works [#how-it-works]

The app is a Homey **Python** app built on
[`homey-esphomedriver`](https://github.com/Doekse/homey-esphomedriver), the shared ESPHome layer that also powers
the generic ESPHome app for Homey. That library handles discovery, pairing, encryption, reconnects and the
standard capabilities. This app adds what is specific to the S1 Pro: zones, live targets, flow cards, the
settings mirror, the zone editor, the radar widget and firmware notices.

Everything runs on your local network. The only outbound request is a check for new firmware on Sensy-One's
GitHub releases page, every six hours.


# Installation (/docs/installation)



## Requirements [#requirements]

|                    |                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Homey**          | Homey Pro (2023) or Homey Pro mini                               |
| **Homey firmware** | 13.0 or newer (the app is a Python app)                          |
| **Sensor**         | Sensy-One S1 Pro Multi Sense, official firmware v1.2.21 or newer |
| **Network**        | Homey reaches the sensor on TCP port 6053                        |

Homey Pro (Early 2019) and older, and Homey Cloud, are not supported.

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="Custom firmware">
    Firmware that keeps the official entity names works as well. The app finds the sensor by its ESPHome project name,
    `Sensy-One.S1 Pro Multi Sense`, so keep that unchanged. It also understands the live target entities of the
    earlier "Homey edition" firmware (`live_t1_x` and so on). Features that need entities a custom build left out
    simply stay empty.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Separate networks and VLANs">
    Automatic discovery uses mDNS (`_esphomelib._tcp`), which does not cross networks or VLANs. If the sensor lives on
    a separate IoT network, add it [by IP address](#add-by-ip-address) and give it a fixed IP address (a DHCP
    reservation in your router).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Internet access">
    Everything stays on your local network. Only the [firmware notice](/docs/maintenance#firmware-updates) needs
    internet access, to check `github.com` for new releases.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

<Callout type="warn" title="Keep the Bluetooth proxy off">
  The official firmware has a Bluetooth proxy for Home Assistant (**BLE | Proxy** on the sensor's web page). The
  ESP32-C3 shares one radio between WiFi and Bluetooth, and with the proxy on the connection to Homey drops
  regularly. The app shows a warning on the device while it is on.
</Callout>

## Install the app [#install-the-app]

<Tabs items="[&#x22;Homey App Store&#x22;, &#x22;Homey CLI&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="Homey App Store">
    Open the app's page in the Homey App Store and choose **Install**. While the app is in testing, use the test link
    from the [project page](https://github.com/starredev/homey-sensy-s1pro). Updates arrive through the App Store.
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Homey CLI">
    You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22, the Homey CLI and
    [Docker](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/), which compiles the app's Python dependencies.

    ```bash
    npm install --global homey
    git clone https://github.com/starredev/homey-sensy-s1pro.git
    cd homey-sensy-s1pro
    homey login
    homey select
    homey app install
    ```

    On Windows, see the [Windows notes](/docs/developers/development#windows) if the CLI fails with *Error while
    collecting cross-compiled virtual environment*.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Add the sensor [#add-the-sensor]

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Start adding a device [#start-adding-a-device]

    In the Homey app, go to **Devices → +**, choose **Sensy S1 Pro**, then **S1 Pro Multi Sense**.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Pick your sensor [#pick-your-sensor]

    Homey lists the S1 Pro sensors it found on your network that are not added yet. Pick yours. Not in the list?
    Choose **Add by IP…** (see below).
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Done [#done]

    Homey connects, reads the sensor and adds the device, named as the sensor reports itself (for example
    *S1 Pro Multi Sense 2cd9f0*). Move it to the room it hangs in, so Homey's zone activity follows it.
  </Step>
</Steps>

Right after adding, the app reads everything from the sensor: the [device values](/docs/device), all
[settings](/docs/settings), and the zones that are already drawn, which get their own capabilities a few seconds
later.

### Add by IP address [#add-by-ip-address]

Use **Add by IP…** when the sensor is not found automatically.

1. Enter the sensor's **IP address or host name**, for example `192.168.1.40` or `s1-pro-multi-sense-2cd9f0.local`.
2. Leave the **port** at `6053` unless you changed it in the firmware.
3. Choose **Connect**.

You find the IP address in your router or on the sensor's web page. A sensor added this way is still recognised by
its MAC address, so if mDNS later sees it at another address, Homey follows it.

### Encryption key [#encryption-key]

If the firmware has an API encryption key (`api: encryption: key:` in ESPHome), Homey asks for it after
connecting. The official firmware has no key, so normally you will not see this step.

### If adding fails [#if-adding-fails]

| Message                                                    | Cause                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| *This ESPHome project is not supported by this Homey app.* | Another ESPHome device answered, or the firmware's project name is not `Sensy-One.S1 Pro Multi Sense`. |
| *Could not connect to the ESPHome device…*                 | Nothing answered on port 6053. Check the address, power and network.                                   |
| *The device did not respond in time.*                      | The sensor is busy or the network is slow. Try again.                                                  |
| *The encryption key is invalid.*                           | The key does not match the firmware.                                                                   |
| *This device is not using encryption.*                     | You entered a key, but the firmware has none.                                                          |

## Change the address later [#change-the-address-later]

If the sensor got a new IP address that Homey does not pick up by itself, or you added an encryption key, open
the device's settings and choose **Repair**. The device, its flows and Insights are kept.

## Coming from the previous version [#coming-from-the-previous-version]

Earlier versions of this app were written in Node.js and had the app id `io.github.starredev.sensys1pro`. The
current app (`io.github.starredev.sensy`) installs **next to** it.

1. Install the new app and add the sensor (both apps can be connected at the same time).
2. Move your flows to the new device. Presence is now `alarm_presence` (was `alarm_motion`), movement is now
   `alarm_motion` (was `sensy_moving`). The app's own flow cards kept their names.
3. Remove the old device and the old app.


# Maintenance and firmware (/docs/maintenance)



## Maintenance actions [#maintenance-actions]

Open the device and find the maintenance actions (in the device's settings, under *Maintenance*).

### Calibrate CO₂ sensor [#calibrate-co-sensor]

Sets the SCD40's CO₂ reading to **426 ppm**, the CO₂ level of outdoor air (forced recalibration).

<Callout type="warn" title="Only in fresh outdoor air">
  The calibration assumes the sensor is in outdoor air **right now**. Put the sensor outside (or at a wide
  open window with a breeze) for **at least 3 minutes** first, without people breathing nearby. Calibrating
  indoors makes every later reading wrong.
</Callout>

Use it when the CO₂ readings have drifted, for example when they stay well above 420 ppm while the room is
thoroughly aired. The firmware does not recalibrate the sensor by itself.

### Restart sensor [#restart-sensor]

Restarts the sensor's ESP32. The device is unavailable for a few seconds and reconnects by itself. Zones and
settings are kept: they are stored on the sensor.

### Restart radar [#restart-radar]

Restarts only the radar module. Use it when the radar stops reporting people while the rest of the sensor
works.

### Refresh capabilities [#refresh-capabilities]

Rebuilds the device's capabilities from what the sensor reports. You rarely need it:

* capabilities for newly drawn zones appear by themselves;
* after an app update that adds capabilities, the device refreshes once by itself.

Use it after a firmware update that added new entities, if they do not show up. Your zone capabilities are kept.

## Firmware updates [#firmware-updates]

The app checks the [Sensy-One releases on GitHub](https://github.com/sensy-one/S1-Pro-Multi-Sense/releases)
when the sensor connects and then every six hours. When a newer version than the one on your sensor is out:

* the device shows a warning: *Firmware vX is available (installed: vY). Update the sensor from its web page.*;
* the [*New firmware is available*](/docs/flows#when) trigger fires, once per version.

The app does **not** install updates itself. Update the sensor from its own web page:

1. Open the sensor's web page (its address is in the device settings under *Web server*, or
   `http://<sensor-ip>/`).
2. Use the firmware update there, following Sensy-One's instructions.

The warning disappears as soon as the sensor reconnects with the new version.

<Callout type="info" title="Why Homey checks instead of the sensor">
  The firmware can check GitHub itself, but the HTTPS request needs a lot of memory on the ESP32-C3 and rarely
  gets an answer. Homey checks instead and only compares version numbers; nothing about your sensor is sent.
</Callout>

## Extra capabilities [#extra-capabilities]

Two switches in the device settings, under *Capabilities*, add more of the sensor's entities to the device:

<Tabs items="[&#x22;Show diagnostic capabilities&#x22;, &#x22;Show configuration capabilities&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="Show diagnostic capabilities">
    | Capability          | From the sensor             |
    | ------------------- | --------------------------- |
    | Connectivity        | ESP32 status                |
    | Temperature (ESP32) | Chip temperature            |
    | IP address          | ESP32 IP                    |
    | WiFi network        | ESP32 SSID                  |
    | WiFi strength       | *Very weak* … *Very strong* |
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Show configuration capabilities">
    | Capability                         | From the sensor                                  |
    | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
    | On/off, brightness, colour, effect | The RGB status LED (WS2812)                      |
    | BLE proxy                          | Bluetooth proxy for Home Assistant (keep it off) |
    | Buzzer                             | The buzzer as a switch                           |
    | Radar Bluetooth                    | The radar module's own Bluetooth                 |
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Turning a switch off removes those capabilities again. Settings that already have a place in the
[device settings](/docs/settings) (single target, mirrored mounting, real-time readings, holding engine, tracking
numbers, offsets, buzzer pitch and volume) and the factory reset buttons are never added as capabilities.

## Factory resets [#factory-resets]

The sensor has factory reset buttons for the ESP32, the radar and the CO₂ sensor. The app deliberately does not
offer them: one tap would wipe your sensor's WiFi, zones or calibration. Use the sensor's own web page if you
really need them.


# Placing the sensor (/docs/placement)



The S1 Pro's mmWave radar sees a **fan-shaped area of about 120°** in front of the sensor. Placement decides
how well it detects people, and where your zones end up.

## The coordinate system [#the-coordinate-system]

The app, the zone editor and the radar widget all use the radar's own coordinates, in centimetres:

```
            y (distance in front of the sensor)
            ▲
     ╲      │      ╱
      ╲     │     ╱     ← about 120° field of view
       ╲    │    ╱
        ╲   │   ╱
 ─x ◀────── ● ──────▶ +x
          sensor
```

* **x** is left (−) or right (+) as seen *from* the sensor.
* **y** is the distance straight in front of the sensor.
* The **detection range** (default 600 cm, see [settings](/docs/settings#detection)) limits how far the
  radar looks.

## Tips [#tips]

* **Face the open room.** Mount the sensor so the area you care about is in front of it, not at the far edge of
  the field of view.
* **Avoid moving objects in view**: fans, curtains in a draught, plants near a heater, robot vacuums. Hide them
  with an [exclusion zone](/docs/zones#the-exclusion-zone) if you cannot avoid them.
* **Be careful with mirrors, glass and tiles.** Radar signals reflect off hard, flat surfaces. A person can then
  show up twice: once where they are and once as a "mirror image" that moves along. Bathrooms with large
  mirrors or a glass shower wall are the worst case. See [ghost targets](/docs/troubleshooting#ghost-targets).
* **Pets are seen too.** A cat or dog is a moving target like any other. Zones and the
  [people count condition](/docs/flows) help to tell a person from a pet in most rooms.
* **Upside down or facing the other way?** Turn on [*Mirrored mounting*](/docs/settings#detection) so left
  and right are not swapped in your zones and on the radar.

<Callout type="info" title="Sensy-One's own guidance">
  For mounting height, angle and the sensor's exact range, follow the instructions that came with the sensor
  and the [Sensy-One documentation](https://github.com/sensy-one/S1-Pro-Multi-Sense).
</Callout>

## Checking the result [#checking-the-result]

Open the [zone editor](/docs/zones) (**Apps → Sensy S1 Pro → Configure**) and walk around the room. You
see yourself as a dot on the radar map. If the dot follows you well everywhere you want to detect people, the
sensor is placed right.


# Capabilities (/docs/reference/capabilities)



Capabilities are mapped by [`homey-esphomedriver`](/docs/developers/esphomedriver) from the sensor's entities,
using the app's brand profile. Device class: **sensor**.

## Always present [#always-present]

| Capability            | Type           | Title                   | Unit     | Insights | Source entity                |
| --------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------------------------- |
| `alarm_presence`      | boolean        | Presence                |          | yes      | `any_presence`               |
| `alarm_motion`        | boolean        | Motion                  |          | yes      | `any_movement`               |
| `sensy_people`        | number (0–3)   | People                  |          | yes      | `all_targets_count`          |
| `measure_temperature` | number         | Temperature             | °C       | yes      | `bme688_temperature`         |
| `measure_humidity`    | number         | Humidity                | %        | yes      | `bme688_humidity`            |
| `measure_pressure`    | number         | Pressure                | mbar     | yes      | `bme688_pressure`            |
| `measure_co2`         | number         | CO₂                     | ppm      | yes      | `scd40_co__concentration`    |
| `sensy_iaq`           | number (0–500) | Air quality (IAQ)       |          | yes      | `bme688_iaq`                 |
| `sensy_air_quality`   | enum           | Air quality             |          | no       | `bme688_iaq_classification`  |
| `sensy_iaq_accuracy`  | enum           | Air quality calibration |          | no       | `bme688_iaq_accuracy`        |
| `measure_tvoc`        | number         | VOC                     | ppm      | yes      | `bme688_voc_equivalent`      |
| `measure_luminance`   | number         | Luminance               | lx       | yes      | `ltr390_ambient_light__lux_` |
| `measure_ultraviolet` | number         | Ultraviolet             | UV index | yes      | `ltr390_uv_index`            |

### Enum values [#enum-values]

`sensy_air_quality`: `Excellent`, `Good`, `Lightly polluted`, `Moderately polluted`, `Heavily polluted`,
`Severely polluted`, `Extremely polluted`. The values are the firmware's own text, so they are also what the
*Air quality* token contains.

`sensy_iaq_accuracy`: `Stabilizing`, `Uncertain`, `Calibrating`, `Calibrated`.

## Per drawn zone [#per-drawn-zone]

`N` is 1, 2 or 3. Present only for zones with an outline of at least three points.

| Capability                  | Type         | Title            | Insights | Source entity         |
| --------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------- | -------- | --------------------- |
| `sensy_zone_presence.zoneN` | boolean      | Zone N presence  | yes      | `zone_N_presence`     |
| `sensy_zone_movement.zoneN` | boolean      | Zone N movement  | yes      | `zone_N_movement`     |
| `sensy_zone_people.zoneN`   | number (0–3) | People in zone N | yes      | `zone_N_target_count` |

## Maintenance actions [#maintenance-actions]

| Capability             | Title                | Presses                       |
| ---------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `button.calibrate_co2` | Calibrate CO₂ sensor | `scd40___forced_calibration`  |
| `button.restart`       | Restart sensor       | `esp32___restart_module`      |
| `button.restart_radar` | Restart radar        | `radar___restart_module`      |
| `button.refresh`       | Refresh capabilities | *(rebuilds the capabilities)* |

## Optional [#optional]

With **Show diagnostic capabilities** or **Show configuration capabilities** on, the library adds the remaining
diagnostic and configuration entities with its generic mapping: `alarm_connectivity`,
`measure_temperature.esp32___temperature`, `esphome_string.esp32___ip`, `esphome_string.esp32___ssid`,
`esphome_string.esp32___wifi_strength`, the LED (`onoff`, `dim`, `light_hue`, `light_saturation`,
`light_effect`) and switches such as `onoff.ble___proxy`, `onoff.mlt8530___buzzer` and
`onoff.radar___bluetooth`. Exact ids can differ slightly when several entities share a base capability.

## Custom capability definitions [#custom-capability-definitions]

The app defines these custom capabilities (in `.homeycompose/capabilities/`):

| Id                    | Type    | Notes                                  |
| --------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `sensy_people`        | number  | 0–3, no decimals                       |
| `sensy_iaq`           | number  | 0–500, no decimals                     |
| `sensy_air_quality`   | enum    | See above                              |
| `sensy_iaq_accuracy`  | enum    | See above                              |
| `sensy_zone_presence` | boolean | Used as `sensy_zone_presence.zoneN`    |
| `sensy_zone_movement` | boolean | Used as `sensy_zone_movement.zoneN`    |
| `sensy_zone_people`   | number  | 0–3, used as `sensy_zone_people.zoneN` |


# Sensor entities (/docs/reference/entities)



The S1 Pro on the official firmware v1.2.21 reports these 151 ESPHome entities. The table shows what the app does with
each of them. Object ids are as `aioesphomeapi` reports them; for names with non-ASCII characters they can differ
from other ESPHome clients (`SCD40 CO₂ Concentration` is `scd40_co__concentration`).

*Category* is the ESPHome entity category: entities without one are primary entities, *config* and *diagnostic*
entities are hidden by default in most ESPHome integrations.

| `any_presence`           | BinarySensor | —        | Capability `alarm_presence` · flows, widget |
| `any_presence_delay`     | Number       | —        | Setting `any_presence_delay`                |

| `esp32___ssid`            | TextSensor   | diagnostic | Capability with *Show diagnostic capabilities*                |
| `esp32___status`          | BinarySensor | diagnostic | Capability with *Show diagnostic capabilities*                |
| `esp32___temperature`     | Sensor       | diagnostic | Capability with *Show diagnostic capabilities*                |
| `esp32___wifi_strength`   | TextSensor   | diagnostic | Capability with *Show diagnostic capabilities*                |
| `mlt8530___buzzer`        | Switch       | config     | *Beep* flow action · capability with *Show configuration*     |
| `mlt8530_buzzer_pitch`    | Number       | —          | Setting `buzzer_pitch`                                        |
| `mlt8530_buzzer_volume`   | Number       | —          | Setting `buzzer_volume`                                       |
| `mode___realtime`         | Switch       | config     | Setting `realtime`                                            |
| `ws2812___led`            | Light        | config     | Capability with *Show configuration capabilities*             |


# Flow cards (/docs/reference/flow-cards)



Every flow card of the app's own, with its id, arguments and tokens. Cards are device cards: they all have a
*device* argument (the S1 Pro). For when to use them, see the [Flows guide](/docs/flows).

Homey also offers its standard cards for the standard capabilities of the device (see [Capabilities](/docs/reference/capabilities)).

## Triggers (When…) [#triggers-when]

### Someone became present [#someone-became-present]

* **Id:** `room_occupied`
* **Card text:** Someone became present
* **Dutch:** Iemand werd aanwezig
* **Token:** `people` (number): People, for example `1`

### The room became empty [#the-room-became-empty]

* **Id:** `room_empty`
* **Card text:** The room became empty
* **Dutch:** De ruimte werd leeg

### Number of people changed [#number-of-people-changed]

* **Id:** `people_changed`
* **Card text:** Number of people changed
* **Dutch:** Aantal personen veranderde
* **Token:** `people` (number): People, for example `2`
* **Token:** `previous` (number): Previous, for example `1`

### Air quality changed [#air-quality-changed]

* **Id:** `air_quality_changed`
* **Card text:** Air quality changed
* **Dutch:** Luchtkwaliteit veranderde
* **Token:** `air_quality` (string): Air quality, for example `Good`
* **Token:** `previous` (string): Previous, for example `Excellent`

### Someone entered a zone [#someone-entered-a-zone]

* **Id:** `zone_entered`
* **Card text:** Someone entered *zone*
* **Dutch:** Iemand kwam *zone* binnen
* **Argument:** `zone` (dropdown, one of: `1` (Zone 1), `2` (Zone 2), `3` (Zone 3))
* **Token:** `people` (number): People in zone, for example `1`

### A zone became empty [#a-zone-became-empty]

* **Id:** `zone_left`
* **Card text:** *zone* became empty
* **Dutch:** *zone* werd leeg
* **Argument:** `zone` (dropdown, one of: `1` (Zone 1), `2` (Zone 2), `3` (Zone 3))

### Movement started in a zone [#movement-started-in-a-zone]

* **Id:** `zone_movement_started`
* **Card text:** Movement started in *zone*
* **Dutch:** Beweging gestart in *zone*
* **Argument:** `zone` (dropdown, one of: `1` (Zone 1), `2` (Zone 2), `3` (Zone 3))

### Movement stopped in a zone [#movement-stopped-in-a-zone]

* **Id:** `zone_movement_stopped`
* **Card text:** Movement stopped in *zone*
* **Dutch:** Beweging gestopt in *zone*
* **Argument:** `zone` (dropdown, one of: `1` (Zone 1), `2` (Zone 2), `3` (Zone 3))

### New firmware is available [#new-firmware-is-available]

* **Id:** `firmware_available`
* **Card text:** New firmware is available
* **Dutch:** Er is nieuwe firmware beschikbaar
* **Hint:** Homey checks the Sensy-One releases every few hours. Update the sensor from its web page.
* **Token:** `version` (string): Version, for example `v1.3.0`
* **Token:** `installed` (string): Installed version, for example `v1.2.21`

## Conditions (And…) [#conditions-and]

### Someone is / isn't present [#someone-is--isnt-present]

* **Id:** `is_present`
* **Card text:** Someone is / isn't present
* **Dutch:** Er is / is niet iemand aanwezig

### Zone is / isn't occupied [#zone-is--isnt-occupied]

* **Id:** `zone_occupied`
* **Card text:** *zone* is / isn't occupied
* **Dutch:** *zone* is / is niet bezet
* **Argument:** `zone` (dropdown, one of: `1` (Zone 1), `2` (Zone 2), `3` (Zone 3))

### There is / is no movement in a zone [#there-is--is-no-movement-in-a-zone]

* **Id:** `zone_moving`
* **Card text:** There is / is no movement in *zone*
* **Dutch:** Er is / is geen beweging in *zone*
* **Argument:** `zone` (dropdown, one of: `1` (Zone 1), `2` (Zone 2), `3` (Zone 3))

### Number of people is / isn't above [#number-of-people-is--isnt-above]

* **Id:** `people_above`
* **Card text:** Number of people is / isn't above *count*
* **Dutch:** Aantal personen is / is niet hoger dan *count*
* **Argument:** `count` (number, 0–3)

### Air quality is / isn't at least as bad as [#air-quality-is--isnt-at-least-as-bad-as]

* **Id:** `air_quality_at_least`
* **Card text:** Air quality is / isn't *level* or worse
* **Dutch:** Luchtkwaliteit is / is niet *level* of slechter
* **Argument:** `level` (dropdown, one of: `Excellent` (Excellent), `Good` (Good), `Lightly polluted` (Lightly polluted), `Moderately polluted` (Moderately polluted), `Heavily polluted` (Heavily polluted), `Severely polluted` (Severely polluted), `Extremely polluted` (Extremely polluted))

## Actions (Then…) [#actions-then]

### Set zone presence hold time [#set-zone-presence-hold-time]

* **Id:** `set_zone_delay`
* **Card text:** Set presence hold time of *zone* to *seconds* seconds
* **Dutch:** Zet vasthoudtijd van *zone* op *seconds* seconden
* **Argument:** `zone` (dropdown, one of: `1` (Zone 1), `2` (Zone 2), `3` (Zone 3))
* **Argument:** `seconds` (number, 0–3600)

### Beep [#beep]

* **Id:** `beep`
* **Card text:** Beep for *duration* seconds
* **Dutch:** Piep *duration* seconden
* **Argument:** `duration` (number, 0.1–5)

## Behaviour [#behaviour]

* Room and zone triggers fire on real changes only. Values the sensor re-sends after a reconnect never fire a card.
* Zone triggers and zone conditions ignore zones without an outline (fewer than three points).
* *Someone entered a zone* reports at least 1 person, because the zone's people count can lag behind its presence.
* *Air quality changed* does not fire for the first class reported after a (re)connect, and ignores the firmware's `error` value.
* *New firmware is available* fires once per release version, and again only for a newer release.
* *Beep* turns the buzzer on, waits, and always turns it off again, also when the flow is stopped in between.


# Settings reference (/docs/reference/settings)



All device settings, with their id, type, range and the sensor entity they mirror. Settings with a sensor
entity are kept in sync in both directions; see the [Device settings guide](/docs/settings) for what they do.

## Detection [#detection]

| Setting                        | Id                       | Type     | Default | Range         | Sensor entity            |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------ | -------- | ------- | ------------- | ------------------------ |
| Detection range                | `detection_range`        | number   | 600     | 0 – 1800 cm   | `detection_range`        |
| Presence hold time             | `any_presence_delay`     | number   | 0       | 0 – 3600 s    | `any_presence_delay`     |
| Movement threshold             | `any_movement_threshold` | number   | 0       | 0 – 5000 cm/s | `any_movement_threshold` |
| Track a single person          | `single_target`          | checkbox | False   |               | `radar___single_target`  |
| Mirrored mounting              | `mirrored`               | checkbox | False   |               | `radar___flip_y_axis`    |
